description: Proposed re-expression of the 89 seed exercises in the new model. Ids unchanged. Flag codes: M meaning of a tag changes; D debatable tag; E equipment tag inaccurate (proposed item); R refinement to a finer node; N note.

flag.text: Classed as squat; a leg press is a machine press with a supported back. Reviewer may prefer a separate pattern.
Secondary calves stands for gastrocnemius.
Secondary calves stands for gastrocnemius.
Glutes and lower back are arguably co-primary with hamstrings. Seed primary kept.
As Romanian deadlift.
Seed primary is glutes alone. Hamstrings and lower back are arguably co-primary. Adding a primary changes attributed set counts, so the owner decides.
As conventional deadlift; adductors tagged secondary.
Hybrid of hinge and squat; hinge listed first. Quadriceps primary is defensible.
Quadriceps as secondary is doubtful; review.
Step-up is classed with lunge and split stance. Equipment: bench in seed; plyoBox is the closer requirement.
Refined to gastrocnemius (primary) and soleus (secondary); standing with the knee straight.
Gluteus medius is the main mover but sits under Glutes; the seed primary abductors holds only tensor fasciae latae. Consider adding gluteusMedius as primary (changes attributed counts).
Incline emphasises the clavicular head only qualitatively. Optional refinement to pectoralisMajorClavicular.
As incline barbell press.
Abs retained as secondary; anti-extension listed as second pattern.
Upper back as secondary stands for upper trapezius.
Triceps and chest are co-primary in practice, depending on lean. Pattern classed as vertical push: debatable.
As dips.
Biceps is arguably co-primary.
Equipment lists cable and machine together; a single class applies at coverage (cable).
Lats arguably co-primary. Row primaries are inconsistent across the seed (upperBack here, lats for one-arm row).
As seated cable row.
Primary lats while barbell and cable rows use upperBack. Harmonise during enrichment.
Equipment lists barbell and squatRack; the barbell is a fixed bar here. Coverage baseline counts it as bodyweight.
Rear delts primary; infraspinatus and middle trapezius are likely co-targets. Second pattern external rotation.
Refined from upperBack to trapeziusUpper; filters by upperBack still match.
Brachialis and brachioradialis emphasis is qualitative. Promoting either to primary would change meaning.
Equipment ezBar and bench; preacherBench proposed.
Front delts as secondary is doubtful; isometric hold.
Abductors secondary stands for gluteus medius, which sits under Glutes.

Category legs; timed isometric squat pattern.
Hip flexors arguably co-primary; front delts as secondary is doubtful.
Primary obliques stands for anti-rotation bracing.
Seed lists no equipment so it shows as bodyweight-only; abWheel proposed.
Category core; forearms primary. Upper trapezius and trunk bracing are co-targets.
Seed tags plate; sled proposed. Category fullBody.
Front delts as secondary is doubtful; hinge listed as pattern (ballistic).
Primary frontDelts understates the lower-body drive. Candidate multiple primaries (changes attributed counts).
Only fullBody target. Consider anatomical secondaries.
Two patterns: squat then vertical push.
Structural near-duplicate of outdoor run; differs by equipment only. Legitimate (equipment) variation.
Primary glutes is a strong claim for incline walking; quadriceps and calves are as defensible.
fullBody primary with lats and quadriceps secondary; acceptable.
Seed lists fullBody as a secondary target. fullBody is non-anatomical and valid only as a primary target, so it moves to primary beside calves.
Near-duplicate of outdoor run and treadmill run by structure. Review for merge or relationship.
As 400 m run.
Seed primary quadriceps; the stretch targets iliopsoas. Primary moves to hipFlexors and quadriceps (rectus femoris) becomes secondary. Primary meaning changes.
Lats primary; lower back and shoulders also lengthen.
Spinal mobility; erector spinae and thoracic spine.
Upper back stands for thoracic spinal extensors and mid-back; lats secondary is doubtful.
Multi-region movement; glutes primary is a choice. Hip flexors and thoracic spine are co-targets.
Deep hip rotators (piriformis) are arguably primary; abductors secondary is doubtful.
